date: after Jumada I 732 AH (Feb 1332); the cipher line is undated
title: One line of numeral cipher under the colophon of a sira manuscript dated 732 AH (BnF Arabe 1966)
place: unknown (Mashriqi hand; Maghribi pieces bound in front)
shelfmark: Paris, BnF, Département des Manuscrits, Arabe 1966
folio_note: Last written page (Gallica view 50, right-hand page, under the colophon): three or four Arabic letters, then about 28 Indian (Arabic-Indic) numerals in one line, in a paler ink than the colophon; two lines of ordinary cursive notes below it. No gloss.
status: De Slane (1883-95), no. 1966: 'Ms. daté de l'an 732 de l'hégire (1332 de J. C.). A la fin du volume se trouve une ligne d'écriture secrète en chiffres indiens.' Seen on the Gallica microfilm scan 15 Nov 2026: the line is there and bare. The 6 Nov 2026 sweep listed the catalogue hit as 'incidental, not opened'. Not on DECODE. Whether the line is as old as the 1332 colophon is not established: the ink is paler and the hand may be a later owner's.
why: If it is of the time of the copy it is one of the oldest unread Arabic numeral cryptograms with an image online; it probably hides a name, a date or an ownership note.
score_note: Scored from the image during the Arabic sweep of 15 Nov 2026, part C (research/sweep_2026-11-15_arabic/); viewed
verify: Order or view the colour scan (the online images are a black-and-white microfilm) to settle the ink and the first letters; try abjad letter values (hisab al-jummal) on the numerals; compare the hand with the owners' notes below it.
